title: DROP COLUMN wrongly escalated to gh-ost on the belief that it requires COPY
migration_snippet:
-- Review note attached to the migration:
--   "DROP COLUMN always requires ALGORITHM=COPY before 8.0.29, so this 5.7
--    table must go through gh-ost."
-- V9__drop_legacy_flag.sql  (MySQL 5.7, 30M rows)
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 3;
ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_flag, ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE;
-- mysqldump of accounts taken and retained for 14 days before this ran
violated_rule: algorithm capability must come from the version matrix, not from memory
expected_feedback: The SQL is correct and the review note is wrong. The official 5.7 matrix lists 'Dropping a column' as In Place = Yes, Permits Concurrent DML = Yes, and the manual's own example is ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN c, ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE. On 8.0 before 8.0.29 the default is INPLACE as well; 8.0.29+ makes it INSTANT. DROP COLUMN is not a COPY operation on any supported version, so routing it to gh-ost adds a ghost table, a cut-over, and hours of runtime for nothing. Note the operation does rebuild the table under INPLACE, so budget the I/O and replica lag — but LOCK=NONE holds and writes continue. The irreversibility of DROP COLUMN is the real risk here, and the retained dump addresses it.
